core_principles.text: Descend into a push-up until your elbows reach an angle of 90 degrees or less, or until your chest touches the floor.
If you cannot descend to an elbow angle of at least 90 degrees, perform push-ups on your knees or with your hands on an elevated platform until strength improves.
Point your hands slightly outward away from your body so your elbows remain close to your torso and stay in alignment with your shoulders.
Maintain a straight body line from the back of your feet to the tip of your head throughout the exercise.
Perform planks on a regular basis to build the core stability required to hold proper alignment during push-ups.
Keep your neck in a neutral position aligned with your spine by focusing your eyes on a spot about a foot in front of you.
Slowing down the repetition speed keeps muscles under tension longer to promote muscle hypertrophy.

common_mistakes.text: Performing a short-range push-up by lowering down only far enough to partially bend the elbows.
Pointing the hands inward during the movement, which causes the elbows to flare outward away from the torso.
Allowing the back and hips to sag toward the floor during the exercise.
Twisting the neck or letting the head drop down while descending.

specific_findings.text: Full range of motion in a push-up requires descending until the elbows reach an angle of 90 degrees or less.
Progression to harder push-up variations is recommended once a lifter can easily complete 20 standard push-ups.
Plyometric clap push-ups activate the pectoralis and triceps muscles to a greater degree than standard push-ups.

consequences.text: Failing to descend to an elbow angle of 90 degrees or less greatly reduces the exercise benefits.
Pointing hands inward and flaring elbows outward places bad alignment on the shoulders and elbows, increasing the risk of shoulder or elbow injury.
Allowing the back and hips to sag breaks straight body alignment and reduces push-up effectiveness.
Twisting the neck or letting it drop places greater stress on the spine and can lead to a neck strain.
